references.text: Pharaoh's magicians said to him: 'This is the finger of God!' – the same expression 'the finger of God' is used for God's direct intervention.
The tablets of the law were written with the finger of God, showing that 'the finger of God' is an expression of God's direct power and action.
The tablets were written with the finger of God – a parallel to the expression 'the finger of God' as a symbol of God's power.
David speaks of the heavens as 'the work of your fingers' – God's finger as an expression of his creative and sovereign power.
Matthew's parallel passage where Jesus says he drives out evil spirits 'by the Spirit of God', while Luke uses 'the finger of God'. Both point to the fact that the kingdom of God has come upon them.
The immediate context in which Jesus drives out an evil spirit and is accused of doing so by Beelzebul – the background for Jesus' statement in verse 20.
Jesus sends out the disciples with the message: 'The kingdom of God has come near to you' – the same message about the coming of the kingdom of God.
Jesus says that the kingdom of God is among you – a parallel to the fact that the kingdom of God has already reached them through Jesus' deeds.
Daniel's prophecy that the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed – the coming of the kingdom of God that Jesus proclaims is the fulfillment of this.
Isaiah's prophecy that God himself will come and save – the exorcisms are signs that God's saving power is at work through Jesus.
